reason: This passage from Exodus 14 (the Red Sea crossing) prominently features the perspective and emotional experience of the Israelite people. The narrative centers on their fear when seeing the approaching Egyptian army, their questioning of Moses and their doubts ('Why have you brought us out to die in the wilderness?'), their cry to God, and their ultimate faith and belief. While the passage includes some omniscient narrative elements (Pharaoh's thoughts, God's actions), the dominant focus remains the experience of ordinary Israelites—enslaved or recently liberated working people—facing existential crisis and divine deliverance. Their concerns, fears, and spiritual response constitute the emotional and narrative heart of the account.
story: The Pharaoh chases after the Hebrews
